topic: Does an individual (non-corporate) owner need a rent increase license?
detail: The license requirement attaches to the OWNER of a rent-controlled unit, not to a corporation. Sec. 37.15(a) says 'Owners of residential dwelling units subject to this Chapter 37 shall be required to report certain information about their units to the Rent Board'. Sec. 37.2(h) defines 'Landlord' as an owner/lessor/sublessor and their agent, representative or successor, with no corporate carve-out. A 1-9 unit building has been covered since March 1, 2023.

topic: Is the license a separate application the owner files with the Rent Board?
detail: The official Housing Inventory page states: 'once you have reported into the Housing Inventory, a rent increase license will be automatically generated for non-owner occupied units.' Reporting is the act that 'informs' the Rent Board; there is no separate license application for annual/banked increases.

topic: Does the owner have to notify the Rent Board about the specific rent increase?
detail: Form 571 states an owner may increase base rent once every 12 months by the allowable amount 'without filing a petition at the Rent Board'. The sf.gov multi-year page confirms 'Landlords are not required to file a petition with the City to impose these types of rent increases'. The license 'does not need to be included with your rent increase notice'. (A petition IS required for the six listed exception categories - see the Requirements page.)

topic: What must be on file with the Rent Board, and when?
value: A CURRENT Rent Increase License, in effect on the increase's EFFECTIVE DATE
detail: sf.gov: 'A current Rent Increase License must be on file with the San Francisco Rent Board before any annual or banked rent increase goes into effect.' Rule 13.14: the effective date, NOT the date of service, is used to decide compliance. So the license must exist before the increase takes effect - not merely before the tenant is notified.

topic: Consequence of an increase taking effect while unlicensed
value: Entire rent increase null and void
detail: Rule 13.14: 'Any rent increase under Ordinance Sections 37.3(a)(1)-(2) purporting to be effective while the landlord is unlicensed shall render the entire rent increase null and void.' Sec. 37.15(e): 'a tenant shall not be obligated to pay the increased rent for months during the period of suspension.' Overpayments may be recoverable by the tenant. Banking rights are preserved.

topic: Does the license prevent a tenant from challenging the increase?
detail: A license is permission to impose an annual/banked increase, not approval of the amount. Tenants may file a Tenant Petition for Unlawful Rent Increase with NO TIME LIMIT and no filing fee, or a Tenant Summary Petition when a notice is clearly unlawful on its face. sf.gov also warns tenants that a license can be granted even where other problems exist.

topic: When did the license requirement start for small buildings?
value: March 1, 2023 for condominiums and buildings with fewer than 10 residential units (July 1, 2022 for 10+ unit buildings)
detail: Sec. 37.15(c) and Rule 13.14 set the phase-in. Note: an official Rent Board form (538) states different dates (7/1/2020 and 3/1/2021) - flagged for review, but the ordinance and Rule 13.14 control here.

A late submission is still accepted and generates a license, but 'your rent increase notice will not be enforceable without having a rent increase license on the effective date of the notice.' The Rent Board does not assess monetary penalties for filing after the deadline.

value: Owner/manager name and business contact; business registration number; approximate square footage; bedrooms/bathrooms; occupancy or vacancy start date; 12-month occupancy history; base rent in $250 increments; utilities included
detail: Reported under penalty of perjury. Owner name and business contact information is PUBLIC in the Housing Inventory. Changes to owner/manager contact information must be updated within 30 days.

topic: Rent Board fee (separate from the license)
value: $59.00 per dwelling unit for 2026-2027; 50% ($29.50) recoverable from the tenant
detail: Paying the fee does not replace Housing Inventory reporting, and reporting does not exempt the fee. Fee is due March 1; a 5% monthly penalty (max 15%) applies after that. 50% of the fee can be recovered from a tenant in occupancy as of November 1 of the applicable tax year.

topic: How to verify the license is active
value: Rent Board Portal - search the address or APN and check the license for the relevant year
detail: Tenants can also look up license status publicly. Check multiple years for all relevant effective dates. A license document appears for units reported as occupied by non-owners.

value: 1 Coverage check > 2 Housing Inventory report > 3 license active > 4 calculate > 5 written notice > 6 effective date (license still current)
detail: Derived strictly from the official steps: coverage (sf.gov), report (S05/S07), license on effective date (S06/S08), calculate on base rent using the rate in effect on the effective date (S01), notice 30/90 days (S01/S30), effective date. This ordering is an editorial synthesis, not a quoted Rent Board instruction.

topic: Free help for owners before filing
value: Rent Board counseling is FREE for tenants and landlords; 415-252-4600
detail: Counselors provide information on the Rent Ordinance but 'cannot give legal advice' and will say when a lawyer is needed. Phone counseling Mon-Fri 9-12 and 1-4; calls generally limited to 5 minutes, office visits to 10 minutes.
Based on 60% of the increase in CPI-U for the Bay Area, capped at 7% by Sec. 37.3(a)(1). Prior periods: 1.4% (3/1/25-2/28/26), 1.7% (3/1/24-2/28/25).

value: The percentage in effect on the DATE THE INCREASE TAKES EFFECT
detail: sf.gov: 'The landlord should use the percentage that will be in effect on the date of the increase, not the percentage in effect on the date they serve the notice.'

topic: Allowable annual increase for March 1, 2027 - February 28, 2028
detail: Not published in any official source consulted as of 2026-11-07. Value intentionally left blank. The Rent Board has also documented a CPI-data issue affecting the 3/1/2026 and 3/1/2027 calculations. Do not estimate.

topic: Does the owner's stated goal ('prevent the rent increase from being challenged') match the law?
detail: No official source states that a license prevents a challenge. The license is a precondition for imposing the increase; challenge rights are independent and have no time limit. The premise should be corrected: see P06.
